GO:0000045.definition: The formation of a double membrane-bounded structure, the autophagosome, that occurs when a specialized membrane sac, called the isolation membrane, starts to enclose a portion of the cytoplasm.
GO:0000045.name: autophagosome assembly

GO:0000149.definition: Binding to a SNARE (soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attached protein receptor) protein.
GO:0000149.name: SNARE binding

GO:0001669.definition: A structure in the head of a spermatozoon that contains acid hydrolases, and is concerned with the breakdown of the outer membrane of the ovum during fertilization. It lies just beneath the plasma membrane and is derived from the lysosome.
GO:0001669.name: acrosomal vesicle

GO:0001675.definition: The formation of the acrosome from the spermatid Golgi.
GO:0001675.name: acrosome assembly

GO:0003723.definition: Binding to an RNA molecule or a portion thereof.
GO:0003723.name: RNA binding

GO:0005096.definition: Binds to and increases the activity of a GTPase, an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of GTP.
GO:0005096.name: GTPase activator activity

GO:0005634.definition: A membrane-bounded organelle of eukaryotic cells in which chromosomes are housed and replicated. In most cells, the nucleus contains all of the cell's chromosomes except the organellar chromosomes, and is the site of RNA synthesis and processing. In some species, or in specialized cell types, RNA metabolism or DNA replication may be absent.
GO:0005634.name: nucleus

GO:0005635.definition: The double lipid bilayer that encloses the nucleus, separating its contents from the cytoplasm. It consists of an inner and outer nuclear membrane, with an intermembrane space (20-40 nm wide, also called the perinuclear space) between them. The envelope is supported by the nuclear lamina and contains nuclear pore complexes, which regulate molecular transport.
GO:0005635.name: nuclear envelope

GO:0005643.definition: A protein complex providing a discrete opening in the nuclear envelope of a eukaryotic cell, where the inner and outer nuclear membranes are joined.
GO:0005643.name: nuclear pore

GO:0005737.definition: The contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.
GO:0005737.name: cytoplasm

GO:0005829.definition: The part of the cytoplasm that does not contain organelles but which does contain other particulate matter, such as protein complexes.
GO:0005829.name: cytosol

GO:0005905.definition: A part of the endomembrane system in the form of an invagination of a membrane upon which a clathrin coat forms, and that can be converted by vesicle budding into a clathrin-coated vesicle. Coated pits form on the plasma membrane, where they are involved in receptor-mediated selective transport of many proteins and other macromolecules across the cell membrane, in the trans-Golgi network, and on some endosomes.
GO:0005905.name: clathrin-coated pit

GO:0006406.definition: The directed movement of mRNA from the nucleus to the cytoplasm.
GO:0006406.name: mRNA export from nucleus

GO:0006886.definition: The directed movement of proteins in a cell, including the movement of proteins between specific compartments or structures within a cell, such as organelles of a eukaryotic cell.
GO:0006886.name: intracellular protein transport

GO:0007289.definition: The specialization of the spermatid nucleus during the development of a spermatid into a mature male gamete competent for fertilization.
GO:0007289.name: spermatid nucleus differentiation

GO:0016032.definition: A multi-organism process in which a virus is a participant. The other participant is the host. Includes infection of a host cell, replication of the viral genome, and assembly of progeny virus particles. In some cases the viral genetic material may integrate into the host genome and only subsequently, under particular circumstances, 'complete' its life cycle.
GO:0016032.name: viral process

GO:0016192.definition: A cellular transport process in which transported substances are moved in membrane-bounded vesicles; transported substances are enclosed in the vesicle lumen or located in the vesicle membrane. The process begins with a step that directs a substance to the forming vesicle, and includes vesicle budding and coating. Vesicles are then targeted to, and fuse with, an acceptor membrane.
GO:0016192.name: vesicle-mediated transport

GO:0019068.definition: A late phase of the viral life cycle during which all the components necessary for the formation of a mature virion collect at a particular site in the cell and the basic structure of the virus particle is formed.
GO:0019068.name: virion assembly

GO:0019080.definition: A process by which a viral gene is converted into a mature gene product or products (proteins or RNA). This includes viral transcription, processing to produce a mature RNA product, and viral translation.
GO:0019080.name: viral gene expression

GO:0019905.definition: Binding to a syntaxin, a SNAP receptor involved in the docking of vesicles.
GO:0019905.name: syntaxin binding

GO:0030136.definition: A vesicle with a coat formed of clathrin connected to the membrane via one of the clathrin adaptor complexes.
GO:0030136.name: clathrin-coated vesicle

GO:0030276.definition: Binding to a clathrin heavy or light chain, the main components of the coat of coated vesicles and coated pits, and which also occurs in synaptic vesicles.
GO:0030276.name: clathrin binding

GO:0031410.definition: A vesicle found in the cytoplasm of a cell.
GO:0031410.name: cytoplasmic vesicle

GO:0034399.definition: The portion of the nuclear lumen proximal to the inner nuclear membrane.
GO:0034399.name: nuclear periphery

GO:0035615.definition: Bringing together a cargo protein with clathrin, responsible for the formation of endocytic vesicles.
GO:0035615.name: clathrin-cargo adaptor activity

GO:0045109.definition: Control of the spatial distribution of intermediate filaments; includes organizing filaments into meshworks, bundles, or other structures, as by cross-linking.
GO:0045109.name: intermediate filament organization

GO:0046784.definition: The directed movement of intronless viral mRNA from the host nucleus to the cytoplasm for translation.
GO:0046784.name: viral mRNA export from host cell nucleus

GO:0060090.definition: The binding activity of a molecule that brings together two or more molecules through a selective, non-covalent, often stoichiometric interaction, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way.
GO:0060090.name: molecular adaptor activity

GO:0072583.definition: An endocytosis process that begins when material is taken up into clathrin-coated pits, which then pinch off to form clathrin-coated endocytic vesicles.
GO:0072583.name: clathrin-dependent endocytosis

GO:0075733.definition: The directed movement of a virus, or part of a virus, within the host cell.
GO:0075733.name: intracellular transport of virus

GO:0120211.definition: Fusion of the membrane of proacrosomal vesicle with the membrane of another proacrosomal vesicle to form the acrosome.
GO:0120211.name: proacrosomal vesicle fusion

GO:0140042.definition: A process that results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts of a lipid droplet.
GO:0140042.name: lipid droplet formation

GO:0140312.definition: Binding directly to the structural scaffolding elements of a vesicle coat (such as clathrin or COPII), and bridging the membrane, cargo receptor, and membrane deformation machinery.
GO:0140312.name: cargo adaptor activity
